subject: Follow-up: Polaris pen-test closure artifacts and runtime access controls
messages:
From: Tom Harper <th@polaris.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Polaris Security Team <security@polaris.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up on pen-test findings #3 & #7 — evidence request

Laura,

Thanks again for walking through the VaultSec report yesterday. The SOC 2 reviewer asked us to collect concrete evidence for two open findings before they sign off:

- Finding #3 (Runtime access controls): proof that token/key access to inference hosts is limited and that ephemeral credentials are used for short-lived processes.
- Finding #7 (S3 object ACLs and audit): confirmation that the problematic bucket has been remediated and object-level ACLs revoked where needed, plus evidence of successful audit runs.

Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD tomorrow (Mar 9)?
- Screenshots showing the runtime role mapping and an example ephemeral credential rotation event
- Minimal config snippet (redacted) showing IAM policy change applied to the bucket in question
- A pointer to the Jira ticket(s) or change request that tracked the remediation
- Any compensating controls (e.g., CloudTrail filters, access logging snapshots) you rely on until auditors close the ticket

If you have a consolidated remediation manifest, that would be ideal. Also copy any internal folks who will own evidence delivery.

Tom
Tom Harper
Security Manager, Polaris Systems
security@polaris.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harper <th@polaris.com>
Cc: Polaris Security Team <security@polaris.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on pen-test findings #3 & #7 — evidence request

Tom — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver what you requested. Summary of next steps from our side:

1) I’ve attached a remediation manifest that maps VaultSec findings to our remediation tickets and owners (polaris_pt_remediation_manifest.pdf).
2) Rishi will capture screenshots and the config snippets; we will redact secrets before sending.
3) We’ll include the Jira ticket link(s) and a short narrative describing compensating controls we had in place during the change window.

Target: we’ll deliver the first package (manifest + screenshots + Jira pointer) by 09:30 PT on Mar 9. If the auditor needs raw logs beyond the screenshots we can provide redacted CloudTrail excerpts.

Cc'ing Neha and Monica — please flag any controls notes you want on the compensating controls section.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: polaris_pt_remediation_manifest.pdf (25 KB, PDF)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harper <th@polaris.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Polaris Security Team <security@polaris.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on pen-test findings #3 & #7 — screenshots and ticket link

Tom / team — attaching the initial artifacts we discussed.

- screenshots_runtime_access.png: two screenshots, (1) role-to-instance mapping in our runtime console, (2) a token rotation event from the last 24 hrs (timestamps included).
- s3_audit_config_snippet.txt: redacted bucket policy and the CLI command we used to remove public ACLs.
- jira-PRJ-473-link.txt: direct link to the remediation ticket (PRJ-473).

Quick notes:
- The runtime uses short-lived certificates issued by our internal CA; the rotation screenshot shows a successful renewal event at 2027-03-09T01:12:34Z.
- The S3 snippet demonstrates we removed the unintended ACL entry and applied a deny statement to public reads; we also kicked off an audit job which is listed in PRJ-473.

If the auditor needs log-level artifacts I can generate a redacted CloudTrail excerpt; that will take an additional hour — let me know.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: screenshots_runtime_access.png (PNG), s3_audit_config_snippet.txt (TXT), jira-PRJ-473-link.txt (TXT)

> - Finding #7 (S3 object ACLs and audit): confirmation that the problematic bucket has been remediated and object-level ACLs revoked where needed, plus evidence of successful audit runs.
>
> Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD tomorrow (Mar 9)?
> ...
From: Tom Harper <th@polaris.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Polaris Security Team <security@polaris.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on pen-test findings #3 & #7 — screenshots and ticket link

Rishi / Laura — received everything, thank you. The screenshots and the Jira pointer look good as a first pass. Quick follow-ups from the SOC reviewer:

- They would like a short artifact showing the recent PR that applied the IAM removal (the PR description is sufficient; you can redact CI tokens).
- For runtime controls, a brief note from your security team describing where ephemeral certs are minted (internal CA vs cloud provider) will help the auditor mark the control as designed and operating.

Can you add those two items to PRJ-473 as comments or attachments? If so, we can move the findings to "pending-auditor-review."

Also, are you able to confirm an estimated date for our SOC 2 auditor to kick off the re-check? Polaris would like to close the loop on their side this week.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Harper
Security Manager, Polaris Systems
security@polaris.com
